## MPPT.dbc

| Device (Source) | Description |
|---|---|
| `Mppt` | The two MPPTs (maximum power point trackers), named Javed and Woof. Each takes power from part of the solar array and converts it to charge the battery. TODO: add the MPPT make and model, and which part of Peri's solar array each MPPT (Javed, Woof) is connected to. |
| `Telemetry` | The telemetry board, which polls the MPPTs (see Telemetry.dbc). |

<a id="mpptpolljaved-0x711"></a>

### MpptPollJaved (0x711)

Request from the telemetry board asking the Javed MPPT to send its status (message Javed). Sent every mppt_update ms (Telemetry/config.txt). The request carries no data.

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Telemetry` |
| CAN ID | 0x711 (1809) |
| Length | 0 bytes |
| Sent every | 1000 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Telemetry/MpptPollJaved"` |

This message carries no data.

<a id="mpptpollwoof-0x712"></a>

### MpptPollWoof (0x712)

Request from the telemetry board asking the Woof MPPT to send its status (message Woof). Sent every mppt_update ms (Telemetry/config.txt). The request carries no data.

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Telemetry` |
| CAN ID | 0x712 (1810) |
| Length | 0 bytes |
| Sent every | 1000 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Telemetry/MpptPollWoof"` |

This message carries no data.

<a id="javed-0x771"></a>

### Javed (0x771)

Status of the MPPT named Javed, sent in reply to each MpptPollJaved request from the telemetry board (every mppt_update ms, Telemetry/config.txt). Not seen in Tests/data/NRT.BIN (iESC 2026 qualifying), although the telemetry board polls both MPPTs every second. TODO: add whether Peri still has these MPPTs; if not, remove this message.

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Mppt` |
| CAN ID | 0x771 (1905) |
| Length | 7 bytes |
| Sent every | 1000 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Mppt/Javed"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OverTemperature` | 1 if the MPPT reports that it is too hot. |  | none |  | 0 = No, 1 = Yes |
| `NoCharge` | 1 if the MPPT reports that it is not charging. TODO: add the conditions that set this flag, from the MPPT datasheet. |  | none |  | 0 = No, 1 = Yes |
| `UnderVoltage` | 1 if the MPPT reports an undervoltage. TODO: add whether this is the solar array (input) or battery (output) side, from the MPPT datasheet. |  | none |  | 0 = No, 1 = Yes |
| `BatteryVoltageLevelReached` | 1 if the battery has reached the MPPT's maximum output voltage, so the MPPT is limiting the charge. |  | none |  | 0 = No, 1 = Yes |
| `VoltageIn` | Voltage from the solar array into this MPPT (scaling from the MPPT datasheet, as previously applied in live_power.py). | V | raw x 0.15049 | 0 to 153.951 |  |
| `CurrentIn` | Current from the solar array into this MPPT (scaling from the MPPT datasheet, as previously applied in live_power.py). | A | raw x 0.00872 | 0 to 8.92056 |  |
| `VoltageOut` | Output voltage of this MPPT (battery side). TODO: add scaling and unit from the MPPT datasheet (still the raw value; check whether it is 208.79 mV per bit, as on similar MPPTs). |  | none |  |  |
| `AmbientTemperature` | Temperature inside this MPPT. TODO: add scaling and unit from the MPPT datasheet (still the raw value). |  | none |  |  |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "OverTemperature" FROM "Mppt/Javed" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

<a id="orion"></a>

## Orion.dbc

| Device (Source) | Description |
|---|---|
| `Orion` | Orion BMS (battery management system). It monitors every cell's voltage, the pack temperatures and the pack current, and switches the pack contactors. Its CAN messages are set up in the Orion BMS utility, so the scaling of every signal depends on the profile loaded on Peri's BMS. |

<a id="packparameters-0x700"></a>

### PackParameters (0x700)

Battery pack summary: current, voltage, state of charge and relay states.

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Orion` |
| CAN ID | 0x700 (1792) |
| Length | 8 bytes |
| Sent every | 500 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Orion/PackParameters"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PackCurrent` | Battery pack current, signed, 0.1 A per bit. NEGATIVE while the battery is supplying current (discharging), positive while it is charging: the opposite of the usual Orion setting. Evidence: the 16 BIN captures in  (Aug to Nov 2026): 53 % of raw values are above 32767, i.e. negative as a signed value; in iESC2026_raceday1.BIN, while the motor controller draws more than 5 A from the DC bus, the pack current is negative in 4068 of 4083 cases and about 0.95 times the bus current (the rest supplied by the solar array). | A | raw x 0.1 | -3276.8 to 3276.7 |  |
| `PackInstVoltage` | Total battery pack voltage, measured right now (instantaneous), 0.1 V per bit. Evidence: in the iESC 2026 recording ESC_2026_0638AM.BIN the raw value ranges from 1103 to 1301 while the motor controller's DC bus voltage ranges from 109.4 to 130.1 V, the usual Orion setting. | V | raw x 0.1 | 0 to 6553.5 |  |
| `PackSoc` | Battery state of charge: how full the battery is, 0.5 % per bit. Evidence: in the iESC 2026 recording ESC_2026_0638AM.BIN the raw value ranges from 11 to 200, i.e. at most 100 %, the usual Orion setting. | % | raw x 0.5 | 0 to 100 |  |
| `RelayState` | Which of the BMS's relay and contactor outputs are on, one bit each. TODO: add the meaning of each bit, from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri. |  | none |  |  |
| `Checksum` | Checksum added by the Orion BMS: in every frame of Tests/data/NRT.BIN (iESC 2026 qualifying) it equals (sum of bytes 0 to 6 + 184) & 0xFF. TODO: add the checksum definition from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri. |  | none |  |  |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "PackCurrent" FROM "Orion/PackParameters" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

<a id="celltempsdcl-0x701"></a>

### CellTempsDCL (0x701)

Discharge current limit and pack temperatures.

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Orion` |
| CAN ID | 0x701 (1793) |
| Length | 8 bytes |
| Sent every | 500 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Orion/CellTempsDCL"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PackDcl` | Discharge current limit: the most current the BMS currently allows to be drawn from the pack, 1 A per bit (the usual Orion setting; not yet confirmed from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri). Evidence: the 16 BIN captures in  (Aug to Nov 2026): always 120. | A | none |  |  |
| `Unknown` | Not known. Evidence: the 16 BIN captures in  (Aug to Nov 2026): 0 to 120, usually 120 (the same as PackDcl), so it may be the charge current limit. TODO: add what the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri sends in bytes 2 and 3 of this message. |  | none |  |  |
| `HighTemperatureSensor` | Highest reading of the pack's temperature sensors, signed, 1 degC per bit (the usual Orion setting; not yet confirmed from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri). Evidence: the 16 BIN captures in  (Aug to Nov 2026): 24 to 43 degC. | C | none | -128 to 127 |  |
| `LowTemperatureSensors` | Lowest reading of the pack's temperature sensors, signed, 1 degC per bit (the usual Orion setting; not yet confirmed from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri). Evidence: the 16 BIN captures in  (Aug to Nov 2026): 11 to 26 degC. | C | none | -128 to 127 |  |
| `Blank` | Not used. |  | none |  |  |
| `Checksum` | Checksum added by the Orion BMS: in every frame of Tests/data/NRT.BIN (iESC 2026 qualifying) it equals (sum of bytes 0 to 6 + 185) & 0xFF. TODO: add the checksum definition from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri. |  | none |  |  |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "PackDcl" FROM "Orion/CellTempsDCL" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

<a id="cellvoltages-0x702"></a>

### CellVoltages (0x702)

Lowest and highest cell voltages in the pack, and the temperature inside the BMS.

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Orion` |
| CAN ID | 0x702 (1794) |
| Length | 8 bytes |
| Sent every | 500 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Orion/CellVoltages"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LowCellVoltage` | Voltage of the lowest cell in the pack, 0.0001 V per bit (the usual Orion setting; not yet confirmed from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri). Evidence: the 16 BIN captures in  (Aug to Nov 2026): 3.33 to 4.39 V; the pack voltage divided by the average cell voltage gives 30 cells in series. | V | raw x 0.0001 | 0 to 6.5535 |  |
| `HighCellVoltage` | Voltage of the highest cell in the pack, 0.0001 V per bit (the usual Orion setting; not yet confirmed from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri). Evidence: the 16 BIN captures in  (Aug to Nov 2026): 3.70 to 4.46 V. | V | raw x 0.0001 | 0 to 6.5535 |  |
| `InternalTemperature` | Temperature inside the BMS unit, 1 degC per bit (the usual Orion setting; not yet confirmed from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri). Evidence: the 16 BIN captures in  (Aug to Nov 2026): 21 to 50 degC. | C | none | 0 to 255 |  |
| `Blank5` | Not used (byte 5). |  | none |  |  |
| `Blank` | Not used (byte 6). |  | none |  |  |
| `Checksum` | Checksum added by the Orion BMS: in every frame of Tests/data/NRT.BIN (iESC 2026 qualifying) it equals (sum of bytes 0 to 6 + 0) & 0xFF. TODO: add the checksum definition from the Orion BMS profile loaded on Peri. |  | none |  |  |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "LowCellVoltage" FROM "Orion/CellVoltages" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

<a id="telemetry"></a>

## Telemetry.dbc

| Device (Source) | Description |
|---|---|
| `Telemetry` | The DUSC telemetry board (Arduino Mega 2560, see Telemetry/README.md). It adds its own GPS and status messages to the CAN bus, and polls the MPPTs. |

<a id="timeandfix-0x0f6"></a>

### TimeAndFix (0x0F6)

GPS date, time and fix status, from the telemetry board's GPS. Sent every gps_update ms (Telemetry/config.txt). The receiver uses it to set the clock for every other message.

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Telemetry` |
| CAN ID | 0x0F6 (246) |
| Length | 8 bytes |
| Sent every | 2000 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Telemetry/TimeAndFix"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GpsHour` | Hour of the GPS time, UTC (0 to 23). | h | none | 0 to 23 |  |
| `GpsMinute` | Minute of the GPS time. | min | none | 0 to 59 |  |
| `GpsSeconds` | Second of the GPS time. | s | none | 0 to 59 |  |
| `GpsDay` | Day of the month of the GPS date. 0 until the GPS has obtained the time. |  | none | 0 to 31 |  |
| `GpsMonth` | Month of the GPS date (1 to 12). 0 until the GPS has obtained the time. |  | none | 0 to 12 |  |
| `GpsYear` | Year of the GPS date, last two digits only (e.g. 26 for 2026). |  | none | 0 to 99 |  |
| `GpsFix` | Whether the GPS has a position fix. |  | none | 0 to 1 | 0 = No fix, 1 = Fix |
| `GpsFixquality` | How the GPS position was obtained (NMEA fix quality). |  | none | 0 to 2 | 0 = Invalid, 1 = GPS, 2 = Differential GPS |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "GpsHour" FROM "Telemetry/TimeAndFix" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

<a id="systemstatusmessages-0x111"></a>

### SystemStatusMessages (0x111)

Telemetry board health. Sent every status_update ms (500 ms in Telemetry/config.txt, as seen in every capture from the car). Most bytes use the codes 0xFF good, 0xAA bad, 0xBB using defaults, 0x00 unknown (see Telemetry/README.md).

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `Telemetry` |
| CAN ID | 0x111 (273) |
| Length | 8 bytes |
| Sent every | 500 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"Telemetry/SystemStatusMessages"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Power` | 0xFF while the board is starting up. After that, the state of the sleep input (pin 33): 1 = car on, 0 = car off. TODO: add what the sleep input (pin 33) is wired to on Peri. |  | none |  | 255 = Starting up, 1 = Car on, 0 = Car off |
| `WritingToSd` | Whether the board is logging every message to its SD card. |  | none |  | 255 = Good, 170 = Bad, 187 = Using defaults, 0 = Unknown |
| `GpsTimeObtained` | Whether the GPS time was obtained at start-up, within time_fix ms (Telemetry/config.txt). |  | none |  | 255 = Good, 170 = Bad, 187 = Using defaults, 0 = Unknown |
| `LoadedConfig` | Whether config.txt was loaded from the SD card (0xFF loaded, 0xBB using defaults). Once the SD log file is open this is replaced by 100 + NN, where the log file is named YYMMDDNN.BIN, or by 90 if the log file could not be opened. |  | none |  | 255 = Good, 170 = Bad, 187 = Using defaults, 0 = Unknown, 90 = Log file could not be opened |
| `Flag` | State of the marker flag input (pin 22), 0 or 1, for marking a moment in the data. TODO: add what the marker flag input (pin 22) is wired to on Peri, and which state means marked. |  | none |  |  |
| `Spare1` | Spare, not used (always 0). |  | none |  |  |
| `Spare2` | Spare, not used (always 0). |  | none |  |  |
| `Spare3` | Spare, not used (always 0). |  | none |  |  |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "Power" FROM "Telemetry/SystemStatusMessages" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

<a id="wavesculptor22"></a>

## wavesculptor_22.dbc

| Device (Source) | Description |
|---|---|
| `Tritium` | Tritium WaveSculptor22 motor controller: drives the motor and reports its speed, currents, voltages and temperatures. Base address 0x300 (messages 0x300 to 0x317), as in Tests/data/NRT.BIN (iESC 2026 qualifying), where it reports device identifier 0x4003 (WaveSculptor22) and serial number 3315. The 2024 car's controller used base address 0x600. TODO: add the controller firmware version. |
| `DriverControls` | Driver controls: send the driver's drive and power commands to the motor controller (base address 0x100), and the current dial setting (0x500). |

<a id="speedvalcurrval-0x101"></a>

### SpeedValCurrVal (0x101)

Drive command from the driver controls to the motor controller: target speed and motor current.

| | |
|---|---|
| From | `DriverControls` |
| CAN ID | 0x101 (257) |
| Length | 8 bytes |
| Sent every | 100 ms |
| InfluxDB measurement | `"DriverControls/SpeedValCurrVal"` |

| Signal (InfluxDB field) | Meaning | Unit | Scaling | Range | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DriverSetSpeed` | Target motor speed requested by the driver controls, in motor rpm (negative = reverse). Evidence: the 16 BIN captures in (Aug to Nov 2026): about 480 rpm while the motor turns at about 330 rpm, i.e. set above the actual speed so that the current request (DriverSetCurrent) controls the car. | rpm | none (sent as a decimal number) |  |  |
| `DriverSetCurrent` | Motor current requested by the driver controls, as a fraction of the controller's maximum current setting (0 to 1, not 0 to 100). Evidence: the 16 BIN captures in (Aug to Nov 2026): 0 to 0.96. |  | none (sent as a decimal number) | 0 to 1 |  |

Example InfluxDB query:

```
SELECT "DriverSetSpeed" FROM "DriverControls/SpeedValCurrVal" WHERE time > now() - 1h
```

<a id="statusinformation-0x301"></a>

| `ErrorFlags` | Error flags, one bit each (bit 0 hardware over current, bit 1 software over current, bit 2 DC bus over voltage, bit 3 bad motor position hall sequence, bit 4 watchdog caused the last reset, bit 5 config read error, bit 6 15 V rail under voltage lock out). 0 = no errors. TODO: add the remaining bits from the WaveSculptor22 user manual. |  | none |  |  |
| `ActiveMotor` | Index of the motor profile currently in use. |  | none |  |  |
| `TransmitErrorCount` | Number of CAN transmit errors counted by the controller. |  | none |  |  |
| `ReceiveErrorCount` | Number of CAN receive errors counted by the controller. |  | none |  |  |
